# tmux / input-fuzzer

tmux's own fuzz target `input-fuzzer` ([source](source/input-fuzzer.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over tmux (tmux/tmux at f763f945).

input_parse_buffer feeds the input (<=512 bytes) to an 80x25 pane's terminal-escape parser, then drains the command queue and runs the libevent loop once.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against tmux at commit f763f945.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- After parsing the input and draining queued commands, the window's reference count is exactly 1 (only the harness's own reference), i.e. input processing leaked no window reference and did not drop one ([lines 62-63](source/input-fuzzer.c#L62-L63)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies it on every input it covers.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v))

**Some statements are blocked by the model.** On the inputs they cover, the binary uses epoll or eventfd, opens files with flags the model does not cover and creates pipes, which this release's model does not decode, so the statements marked "blocked by the model" are false in this model for that reason alone. The program is not at fault.
